title: Seal messages with AES-GCM

blocks.text: The page's `AesGcmExample` encrypts with `AES/GCM/NoPadding`: a 12-byte IV, a 128-bit authentication tag, and three rules. **Each encryption draws a fresh random IV**: reusing an IV with the same key is catastrophic. The IV is not secret, and **it travels in front of the ciphertext**, so any holder of the key can decrypt later. And GCM is authenticated: **a tampered box is refused** with an exception, never decrypted into garbage.

items: `seal(plaintext)` returns `IV (12 bytes, from random) + ciphertext + tag`;
`open(box)` returns the plaintext, and throws `AEADBadTagException` when the box was changed.

rows: 12 + 29 + 16 = 57 bytes; the first 12 are the IV
`open(box)` after one byte of `box` is flipped

cases.says: open(seal(m)) gives back "Contract: Alice pays Bob $100", and an empty message round-trips too.
Sealing the same message twice gives boxes with different IVs.
A box is 12 + 29 + 16 bytes, starts with the 12 bytes the random gave, and another AesBox with the same key opens it.
Flipping one bit of the ciphertext makes open() throw AEADBadTagException.

concepts: AES-GCM gives confidentiality and integrity: a fresh random 12-byte IV per encryption, prepended to the ciphertext, and a tampered ciphertext fails decryption.
SecureRandom, never Random or Math.random(), supplies keys, IVs and tokens.
